meta.title: Colombian Coffee Origins
meta.description: Source specialty coffee directly from Colombian producers.

hero.subtitle: Green coffee lots for roasters around the world, and roasted coffee from the farms for cafés and homes in Colombia.
hero.photoAlt: Coffee plants with ripe red cherries on misty Colombian mountains

farmers.text: Every coffee we offer comes from family farmers and local producers: people who grow great coffee and are proud to share it with the world. We work with them directly, so their name, their farm and their story travel with every lot.

points.title: Family farms
points.text: Small plots, cared for by the families who live on them.

points.title: Local know-how
points.text: Growers who know their land, their varieties and their harvest.

points.title: A name behind every lot
points.text: You always know who grew your coffee, and where.

farmers.imageAlt: Smiling coffee picker with a harvest basket among coffee plants on a Colombian hillside

lots.text: Traceable microlots from family farms high in the Antioquia mountains. Each lot shows its producer, variety, process and cup profile, and you can request a sample before you buy.
lots.note: Example listings for this design preview.

shop.text: A multi-brand shop for Colombian producers who roast their own coffee. Buy bags directly from the farms, for your café or your home.
shop.note: Example products and brands for this design preview.

story.mid: with roasters, coffee shops and importers who care where their coffee comes from.
story.em2: Every producer keeps their own name

facts.text: Mountains, altitude and hundreds of thousands of family farms make Colombia one of the world's great coffee origins.

items.label: coffee-growing families
items.text: Coffee is a family business: most of the country's growers are smallholders.

items.label: bags in the 2024 harvest
items.text: Colombia's biggest crop since 1992, according to the coffee growers' federation.

items.label: Arabica
items.text: Colombia grows Arabica coffee, the species behind almost all specialty coffee.

items.label: harvests a year
items.text: Close to the equator, many regions have a main crop plus a smaller “mitaca”.

items.label: above sea level
items.text: High altitude means cooler nights and slower ripening, which builds sweetness and acidity.

items.label: points = specialty
items.text: On the SCA 100-point cupping scale, coffees scoring 80 or more are graded specialty.

facts.sources: Sources: Federación Nacional de Cafeteros (2024 harvest and grower figures, as reported by Radio Nacional and Valora Analitik); Specialty Coffee Association grading scale.

regions.text: We start where we know every road and every farm. Urrao is our first origin; more Colombian regions are on the way.
regions.photoAlt: The church on Urrao's main square, with its orange spire against a blue sky
regions.description: A mountain town at the edge of the Páramo del Sol: high altitude, cool nights, family farms, and home of the rare Chiroso variety.

producersBand.text: Free basic profile. We verify your farm, photograph your coffee and connect you with buyers.

green.title: List your green coffee lots
green.text: Reach roasters and importers abroad. We handle samples and help with export.

roasted.title: Sell your roasted coffee
roasted.text: Have your own brand? Sell your bags in our shop to cafés and homes across Colombia.

closing.text: Tell us the variety, process, profile and volume you need, and we'll match you with producers within days.

footer.tagline: Specialty coffee sourced directly from Colombian family farms, starting in Urrao, Antioquia. Traceable lots, samples before you buy, export support.
